10863.author: fwyzard
10863.body:
* Re-acquire jobserver tokens periodically.

The wrapper asks for tokens at startup, and then again every `HIPCC_PARALLEL_JOBSERVER_RETRY` seconds (default 10), for as long as there is still an architecture waiting for a slot.

* Support the new offloading driver.

`--offload-new-driver` packages the per-architecture bitcode instead of bundling it, so the wrapper fell back to a serial compile. Detect the pipeline from -### and split it too. The host compile now runs after the packager rather than alongside the device compiles, since it consumes their output.  The new driver can parallelise also the LTO linking step.
10863.title: Update `hipcc-parallel` [new driver]

10864.author: fwyzard
10864.body:
Enable the new offload compiler driver and disable LTO partitions:

The new offload driver can run multiple device LTO compilations in parallel.
Together with LTO partitions this could end up using more processes than requested by the jobserver.

LTO partitions have also been reported to result in a potential performance loss over 10%.

Both options are expected to be the new default in ROCm 10.1.
10864.title: Enable the new offload driver for hipcc

51008.author: rtschmitz
51008.body:
#### PR description:

This PR adds the following changes to NNvtx models:

- Weight, pattern, and association [tensorflow models](https://github.com/cms-data/L1Trigger-L1TTrackMatch/pull/4) have been replaced by hls4ml, including updates to emulator to match model quantization of QKeras training
- NN weight replaces pT in the output VertexWord when running NN vertexing (before: only vertex field filled)
- In case the output of the NNvtx location results in a tie between two bins, a new tiebreaking procedure has been developed. Before, an average was taken between each of the tied bins. Now, the most central bin is chosen in the case of a tie.

#### PR validation:

HW tests have shown 100% agreement with this new emulation. The new vertex bin tiebreak procedure has shown equal or better performance in emulation, with better timing performance on HW. Results have been presented in a [recent GTT meeting](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1689858/#119-e2ennvtx-updating-emulator).
51008.title: [L1T] Update NNVtx emulator to match latest HW (Phase 2)

51705.author: agrubercms
51705.body:
#### PR description:

This PR introduces a new Phase-2 tau HLT path (HLT_DoubleMediumPFPuppiParTTauh30_eta2p1) based on a ParticleTransformer model. The model (+documentation) can be found in [this PR](https://github.com/cms-data/RecoBTag-Combined/pull/73) to the cms-data repository. It was developed to also be able to be used for b-tagging, but was not yet tested for this purpose - to illustrate this, the PR includes b- and c- discriminators, which are currently commented out. Most implementation choices were made to maintain compatibility with the existing tools used by the BTV group (most notably the [hltupler](https://gitlab.cern.ch/cms-btv/hltupler/) framework to produce the training ntuples).
Development progress and measurements were presented regularly in Tau internal meetings, e.g. [here](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1697900/contributions/7139864/attachments/3295080/5892805/ParT_DPSNote_v1.pdf) and [here](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1697959/contributions/7223199/attachments/3325785/5955985/HLT_ParT_progress_260810.pdf). 

The new model significantly outperforms the existing DeepTau model across all evaluated metrics - these are tau tagging efficiency, trigger rate and computational runtime. 

#### PR validation:
The standard tests have been run: 
- `scram b runtests use-ibeos`
- `runTheMatrix.py -l limited -i all --ibeos`

Model performance has been evaluated using the same sample composition as was used in the training, but with a different subgroup of the samples to ensure evaluation is done on events not used in the model training. 

To test this PR, the [PR](https://github.com/cms-data/RecoBTag-Combined/pull/73) to cms-data (mentioned above) containing the onnx model would need to be included.
51705.title: Add HLT_DoubleMediumPFPuppiParTTauh30_eta2p1 path

51866.author: GNiendorf
51866.body: #### PR description: Improves LSTs displaced efficiency with three commits: 8604ed608d4a3a02986f98c92af0c12969dbead6: In the T5 duplicate removal, the pixel cross-clean and promotion used delta-R or an r-z table tuned for prompt tracks. They now use shared hits, such that two T5s are duplicates at 5 shared hits with agreeing embeddings or 10 outright. Also, a pixel object deletes a T5 only if it is promoted and owns 4 of its OT hits. Lastly, a T5 failing the r-z tight cut is promoted if its DNN score passes the 93% retention working point. d1ebda67a70244a1090a160e2378ad850e2e8200: The segment dPhiChange window previously assumed a beam-line origin. It is replaced by an origin-free line residual at 0.75 sigma. The triplet pointing constraint is widened, allowing an additional set of triplets to pass with a special label; such triplets are used only in T5s. a2d88dd2240b44d599101b2566f2814e6356ecc8: The anti-prompt dxy veto and the delta-R duplicate clause are removed, the r-z chi2 ceilings are loosened, and the cross-clean deletes on shared hits with a promoted candidate (3, or 2 for a pT5) instead of direction. A new cut was also introduced, where each flat-barrel mini-doublet's two-hit direction must agree with the parent triplet's circle tangent within 6 sigma of the strip resolution; computed once per triplet, stored as a flag. c.c @slava77

51907.author: JanGerritSchulz
51907.body:
#### PR description:

This PR is removing the non-extended Patatrack configuration for HLT Phase-2. This includes the procModifier `hltPhase2LegacyTrackingPatatrackQuads` that activates the tracking variant, all its custom HLT module configurations, and the related runTheMatrix workflow.

At the moment, there are two legacy tracking configurations supported for HLT Phase-2:
- **`hltPhase2LegacyTracking`** : Legacy HLT tracking from the TDR (2 iterations of Legacy Pixel Seeds + CKF).
- **`hltPhase2LegacyTrackingPatatrackQuads`** : same as previous, but replaces the seeding of the first iteration by (non-OT-extended) Patatrack pixel tracks.

Both legacy configurations are not actively used for development but instead are mainly kept as a reference baseline. They show very similar performance physics-wise (see [comparison validation plots here](https://jaschulz.web.cern.ch/Plots/TrackingPOG/procModifiersSep26/TTbar_200PU/LegacyComparison/)), and are largely outperformed by the current default HLT tracking in most phase-spaces. Due to the similar physics performance, keeping one as a reference should be sufficient. The choice to keep the "legacy" Legacy one is based on the fact that it is still frequently used as a reference in DP notes and internal meetings. 
Removing "Patatrack" Legacy simplifies maintenance and the integration of new developments. It also is in line with the efforts to reduce the number of unneeded procModifiers in the HLT menu as discussed in https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/issues/51817 and as followed-up in the [HLT Upgrade meeting](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1726810/).

#### PR validation:

I ran a limited amount of tests locally using:

```bash
runTheMatrix.py -l ph2_hlt -i all --ibeos
```

51917.author: mmusich
51917.body:
#### PR description:

In view of subsequent work for Phase-2 alignment, this PR introduces `FastDMRChecker`, a new lightweight `EDAnalyzer` for computing DMRs/DRnRs (and by-layer/by-disk residual-pull histograms) without the full overhead of `DMRChecker`. Also factors the code shared between the two into a new header-only library, `interface/DMRHelper.h`.

**New: `plugins/FastDMRChecker.cc`**
- Computes DMRs, DRnRs, and split-DMRs for BPix/FPix/TIB/TOB/TID/TEC.
- Also books by-(subdet, layer/disk) residual and pull histograms across all six subdetectors, using `findSubdetAndLayer()` + a lazily-booked `HistoSet`.

**New: `interface/DMRHelper.h`**
- Shared `Estimators`/`EstimatorMap`/`updateOnlineMomenta()` (running mean/variance), `findSubdetAndLayer()`, `fillByLayer()`, `bookSplitDMRHistograms()`.
- Binning differences between `FastDMRChecker` and `DMRChecker` expressed via a `Traits` template parameter (`DefaultDMRBinning` / `FullDMRBinning`) rather than duplicated functions.

**`plugins/DMRChecker.cc`:** migrated onto `DMRHelper.h` for the pieces that were exact duplicates (`running` namespace, `updateOnlineMomenta`, `bookSplitDMRHistograms`, `cmToUm`). Its `bookResidualsHistogram()`/`fillByIndex()` (pixel-only, pre-booked, with clamping) were left untouched since they behave differently from `fillByLayer()`  no functional change to `DMRChecker`'s existing output.


#### PR validation:

- [x] Clean `scram b` of `Alignment/OfflineValidation`
- [x] Ran existing `DMRChecker`/`FastDMRChecker` test cfg(s) on a small sample, diffed output histograms against `master` for `DMRChecker` (expect no diff)
- [x] Confirmed new `FastDMRChecker` by-layer histograms are populated/sane
- [x] Grepped for other users of removed symbols (`running::`, member `bookSplitDMRHistograms`/`updateOnlineMomenta`/`findSubdetAndLayer`)

#### Backport:

Not a backport.
51917.title: Add `FastDMRChecker` plugin and factor shared code with `DMRChecker` into `DMRHelper.h`

51924.author: mmusich
51924.body:
#### PR description:

This PR removes every dependence of the Phase-2 HLT menus (`HLT_75e33_cff`, `HLT_75e33_timing_cff`, `HLT_NGTScouting_cff`, and therefore `HLT_75e33_trackingOnly_cff`) on EventSetup configuration fragments owned by the offline reconstruction packages. Until now the menus loaded ~40 `cfi`/`cff` files from `RecoTracker`, `RecoLocalTracker`, `RecoLocalCalo`, `TrackingTools`, `TrackPropagation`, `RecoJets` and `CalibMuon`, so that any change made there for offline reconstruction silently changed the HLT menu as well. The menus now only load `Configuration/StandardSequences/Accelerators_cff` and the HLT-owned fragments in `HLTrigger/Configuration/python/HLT_75e33/eventsetup/`, as the Run-3 menus do.

Details:
- Every `ESProducer`/`ESSource` previously pulled in from RECO is now defined in its own `cfi` under `HLT_75e33/eventsetup/`, with the parameters it has in the Phase-2 menu once the era modifiers are applied (e.g. `phase2_tracker`, `trackingPhase2PU140`, `phase2_hgcal`, `run2_HCAL_2017`). The four HLT-owned fragments that were never loaded (`hltESPMeasurementTracker`, `hltESPRKTrajectoryFitter`, `hltESPRKTrajectorySmoother`, `hltESPKFFittingSmootherWithOutliersRejectionAndRK`) were updated to the Phase-2 values and are now used; `hltESPGlobalDetLayerGeometry` is loaded as is.
- Module labels and `ComponentName`s use the Run-3 HLT naming (`hltESP*`, `hltESS*`) wherever the product is only referenced from the configuration, and all consumers (modules and PSets) are updated accordingly, e.g. `WithTrackAngle`  `hltESPTTRHBuilderWithTrackAngle`, `PixelCPEGeneric`  `hltESPPixelCPEGeneric`, `FlexibleKFFittingSmoother`  `hltESPFlexibleKFFittingSmoother`, `MeasurementTracker` (empty `ComponentName`)  `hltESPMeasurementTracker`. The four tracking components with offline names already present in the menu (`initialStepChi2Est`, `highPtTripletStepChi2Est`, `highPtTripletStepTrajectoryCleanerBySharedHits`, `muonSeededTrajectoryCleanerBySharedHits`) get the `hlt` prefix too.
- Five RECO modules were identical to HLT ones already in the menu and are merged into them (`ttrhbwr`, `KFUpdatorESProducer`, `RungeKuttaTrackerPropagator`, `pixelTrackCleanerBySharedHits`, `fwdGsfElectronPropagator`). Six modules that the RECO `cfi`s define only as a side effect of their imports and that nothing in the menu references are dropped (`clusterShapeHitFilterESProducer`, `tkTransientTrackingRecHitBuilderESProducer`, `navigationSchoolESProducerParabolicMf`, `TTRHBuilderFast`, `RKFittingSmoother`, `PropagatorWithMaterialForLoopersOpposite`).
- 20 modules keep their offline label and `ComponentName` on purpose: `SteppingHelixPropagatorAny`, `TransientTrackBuilderESProducer`, `ClusterShapeHitFilterESProducer`, `AnyDirectionAnalyticalPropagator`, `MaterialPropagator`, `OppositeMaterialPropagator`, `MaterialPropagatorParabolicMF`, `navigationSchoolESProducer`, the six `*DetIdAssociator`s, and the producers whose product carries no data label (`CSCChannelMapperESProducer`, `CSCIndexerESProducer`, `CaloTowerConstituentsMapBuilder`, `ecalSeverityLevel`, `hcalRecAlgos`, `hcalChannelPropertiesESProd`). Their product names are hardcoded in C++ (e.g. `MuonIdProducer`, `TrackAssociatorParameters`, `ClusterShapeTrajectoryFilter`, `CkfTrackCandidateMakerBase`, `SeedFromProtoTrack`, the b-tagging and vertexing plugins) or are the defaults of parameters a configuration may leave unset, so the product cannot be renamed; and a module delivering the same product as an offline one has to carry the same label, otherwise the two conflict (`EventSetupConflict`) whenever the HLT fragment runs in the same process as the DIGI or RECO sequences. This is the same set of exceptions the Run-3 menus have.
- `hltESPPhase2StripCPE` delivers its product as `Phase2StripCPEHLT` (via `appendToDataLabel`, since `ComponentType` fixes both the plugin and the product label), so it does not clash with the offline `phase2StripCPEESProducer`.
- `hltMeasurementTrackerEvent` drops the Run-2/3 `siStripDigis` inactive-strip label and the unset `mightGet`.

No change is expected in the HLT results: the configuration is identical to the previous one up to the renaming of EventSetup products described above. The labels of EventSetup modules in the HLT configuration dumps change, so customisations referring to the old offline labels (e.g. `process.MeasurementTracker`, `process.ttrhbwr`) need to be updated.

No dependence on other PRs or externals.

#### PR validation:

- The full configuration of the four menus was dumped (`dumpPython` of every `ESProducer`/`ESSource`, `EDProducer`/`EDFilter`/`EDAnalyzer` and top-level `PSet`) before and after the change, with the `Phase2C17I13M9` and `Phase2C26I13M9` eras: after applying the intended rename map, the 93 EventSetup modules, 712 ED modules and 38 PSets are identical, and the four menus carry identical EventSetup content.
- Every renamed product name was checked against a scan of all quoted string literals in the C++ sources at the base commit, to make sure no plugin fetches it by a hardcoded name.
- `cmsRun` of the Phase-2 HLT step (`DIGI,...,HLT:75e33`) [`ph2_hlt` matrix] runs successfully.

51927.body: #### PR description: A patch for updating the L1 seed used in the Phase-2 `HLT_Photon187` path. The goal is to migrate the L1 seed filtering from the current `L1TTkEmFilter` implementation to the P2GT-based filtering. The new filter uses the `pSingleEGEle51` algorithm from `l1tGTAlgoBlockProducer` for the single photon L1 seed. #### Description of the current changes: The updates include: * Adding `hltEGL1SeedsForSinglePhotonNonIsolatedFilter`, using `HLTP2GTSingleObjectFilter` with the `pSingleEGEle51` P2GT algorithm and `CL2Photons` collection. * Replacing `l1tTkEmSingle51Filter` with the new P2GT-based L1 seed filter in both `HLTPhoton187L1SeededSequence` and `HLTPhoton187UnseededSequence`. * Removing the corresponding `l1tTkEmSingle51Filter` configuration, which is no longer used by the `HLT_Photon187` sequences. #### PR validation: The PR has been prepared starting from `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-09-17-1100`: ```bash cmsrel CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-09-17-1100 cd CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-09-17-1100/src cmsenv git cms-init git cms-addpkg HLTrigger/Configuration scram b && scram b code-checks && scram b code-format && scram b ``` #### Phase-2 HLT validation: The HLT efficiencies before and after the PR were compared as a function of $p_T$ in the barrel region using sample `/RelValZEE_14/CMSSW_20_0_0-PU_150X_mcRun4_realistic_v1_STD_D121_RegeneratedGS_PU_16Aug26-v6/GEN-SIM-RECO` under geometry `ExtendedRun4D121`, and no significant difference was observed.

51939.author: kpedro88
51939.body:
#### PR description:

The easiest way (in terms of minimizing hacks in `Configuration/PyReleaseValidation`) to satisfy #49776 turned out to be adding a local MinBias GEN-SIM step *by default* to all upgrade PU workflows, and then removing it if a default RelVal dataset is specified.

To avoid upsetting special workflows that modify steps/inputs/outputs by assuming fixed numerical indexing of steps, the added MinBias step is injected at the beginning of the workflow and treated as "step 0", to avoid incrementing the indices of other steps. The need for this hack highlights that the planned CMSSW_21_X reimplementation of runTheMatrix should treat multi-step workflows as a DAG (since each step has potentially multiple inputs and/or outputs, which should be chained automatically).

Some other hacks are actually now removed in favor of this approach, namely the previous implementation of the hybrid PU workflows, which also generate MinBias locally.

An option `--noLocalPU` is added to `runTheMatrix.py`, since this development is aimed at PR testing and not actual RelVal submission. @cms-sw/pdmv-l2 should comment if they would prefer something different to minimize the impact on their operations.

I also fixed a very minor bug in the Run4 PU workflow naming and streamlined a few miscellaneous pieces of logic.

It should be kept in mind that 10 MinBias events are enough to test technical functionality of code, but not enough to produce reasonable physics output comparisons.

#### PR validation:

Tested the following workflows, covering all special upgrade workflows that modify PU steps specifically: `37834.0,37834.21,37834.6199,37834.61299,37861.97,37834.99,37834.9921,38634.0,38634.21,38634.6199,38634.61299,38661.97,38634.99,38634.9921,18634.0,18634.96`.

This covers D127 (where a default dataset was specified) and D128 (where a default dataset was not specified), to test both cases. The added local MinBias step is correctly removed by the matrix for D127 and kept for D128. The special workflows tested are: ProdLike, premixing, ECAL devel w/ premixing, and variations/combinations of these.

I also tested with 2026 (Run 3), just the default and hybrid PU workflows. I commented out the default dataset for 2026 to perform this test. The listed Run 3 default datasets are still pre-CMSSW20, so they do not actually work in the modern releases.

51966.author: jprendi
51966.body:
#### PR description:

This PR:

1) separates `hltScoutingDqmOffline` into `hltDqmScoutingAndReco` and `hltDqmOnlyScouting`, such that we could run `hltDqmOnlyScouting` for offline DQM analysis on HLT Scouting Collections without needing prompt results

2) introduces `onlinehlt4vector`, such that we can run the online hlt dqm client in an offline analysis

#### PR validation:

This PR was prepared in `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-09-23-1100`. We can now run the workflows for example like:

```
cmsDriver.py step2 \
    -s DQM:hltDqmOnlyScouting \
    --conditions 160X_dataRun3_NGT_v6 \
    --data \
    --datatier DQMIO \
    -n 100 \
    --eventcontent DQMIO \
    --geometry DB:Extended \
    --era Run3_2026 \
    --filein "${ALL_FILES}" \
    --fileout file:step2.root \
    --nThreads 24 \
    --python_filename dqm.py \
    --no_exec


cat <<@EOF >> dqm.py
process.source.inputCommands = cms.untracked.vstring(
    'keep *',
    'drop CTPPSDiamondDigiedmDetSetVector_hltCTPPSDiamondRawToDigi_TimingDiamond_HLTX',
    'drop CTPPSPixelDigiedmDetSetVector_hltCTPPSPixelDigis__HLTX',
    'drop CTPPSRecord_hltOnlineMetaDataDigis__HLTX',
    'drop DCSRecord_hltOnlineMetaDataDigis__HLTX',
    'drop OnlineLuminosityRecord_hltOnlineMetaDataDigis__HLTX',
    'drop recoBeamSpot_hltOnlineMetaDataDigis__HLTX',
)

process.scoutingCollectionMonitor.onlineMetaDataDigis = "hltOnlineMetaDataDigis"
process.scoutingCollectionMonitor.onlyScouting = True
process.scoutingCollectionMonitor.beamSpot = cms.InputTag("hltOnlineBeamSpotFromDB")
process.ScoutingTrackMonitor.beamSpotLabel = cms.InputTag("hltOnlineBeamSpotFromDB")
@EOF
```

and 

```
cmsDriver.py step2 -s DQM:onlinehlt4vector \
	     --conditions 160X_dataRun3_NGT_v6 \
             --datatier DQMIO \
             -n 100 \
             --eventcontent DQMIO \
             --geometry DB:Extended \
             --era Run3_2026 \
             --filein $ALL_FILES \
             --fileout file:step2.root \
             --nThreads 24 \
             --python_filename dqm.py \
             --no_exec
```

with the subsequent standard harvesting.  It was tested w files produced in `16_0_X`, however when one drops the corresponding collections, this runs fine.

51975.body: #### PR description: This PR was originally #50908. I have commandeered it as the original author has now left CMS. I then fixed the merge conflicts in order to get this into CMSSW. This is the original PR description: * Added valid bit to TkJetWord object * TkJetWord now contains 64 bits of data as opposed to 63 before * Changed track jet ordering on readout to GTT pattern file to reflect the same order as the firmware (was sorted by pT before, now sorted first by phi then by eta) * Added extra output file when running createFirmwareInputFiles_cfg.py called FirmwareGeometryFile.vh. If any of the JetFinding parameters change like eta bin centers or cuts on track multiplicity, regenerate FirmwareGeometryFile.vh and place it in the /algo/components/jet/firmware/hdl/ directory of the JetFinding firmware. * Presentation of changes in a talk coming soon #### PR validation: Original validation: * Valid bit present in track jet words in GTT test vector files * Used FirmwareGeometryFile.vh in the firmware and checked emulator test vector output against firmware. They match. New validation: Ran: * scram b distclean * scram b -j 8 * scram build code-checks * scram build code-format The L1T Menu team saw that the TkJet Performance changed with this PR. [I ran a validation to confirm that this was due to changing the minimum track pT for the tracks considered in the TkJet to 10 GeV](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1728721/#10-tracks-vertex). This is required to match the current FW.
